title: block ticket T-102 on a CI runner sync booked across two servers
goal: Ticket T-102, the nightly build failure, waits on the CI runner owners. Using both MCP servers, book 2026-10-12T11:00 on the calendar as 'CI runner sync' and set T-102 to blocked on the tickets server; initialize and discover the tools of each server separately, read both values back to verify, then report the ticket status and the booked slot.

gold.intent: initialize the tickets session; its result reports the protocol version and capabilities to expect
initialize succeeded on tickets; send notifications/initialized so that server accepts every later request
list the tickets tools and read the first page of schema entries; a nextCursor would mean more pages
the tickets listing continues at the captured cursor; read the second page so the set_status and get_status schema entries are known
the calendar server is a separate session; initialize it too and check its result names calendar, not tickets
the calendar initialize result arrived; send notifications/initialized to the calendar server as well
list the calendar tools on their own server and read their schema before booking anything
read ticket T-102 on the tickets server to confirm it is the nightly build failure the goal names
the ticket note says it fails only on the CI runner; book the CI runner sync on the calendar server with the slot and title the schema names
the booking tool result reported stored; set T-102 to blocked on the tickets server because the ticket now waits on the sync
read the calendar slot back to verify the sync booking is held by the calendar server
read the ticket status back on the tickets server to verify blocked was stored
both read-backs show the expected values; report the ticket status and the booked slot

recovery.intent: the calendar's first page listed no tools but gave nextCursor cursor-0; follow the cursor to read the real page
tickets sent notifications/tools/list_changed and answered -32602; re-list its tools from the first page to read the current schema
the refreshed first page ended with a nextCursor; read the second page, where set_status is listed
the refreshed schema names the ticket by ticket_id instead of id; call set_status again with the renamed argument
